summary: PowerShell modules choose their default interpreter by shebang: #!powershell targets Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows but pwsh elsewhere, and #!/usr/bin/pwsh targets PowerShell 7 everywhere. Custom pwsh shebangs on non-Windows aren't officially supported, so use #!/usr/bin/pwsh and ansible_pwsh_interpreter.
questions: Which shebang should my PowerShell module use for PowerShell 7?
What does #!powershell mean on a Linux target?
Can I use a custom shebang path for pwsh modules?
How do I write a module that must work on older Windows without PowerShell 7?

answer_card.title: PowerShell module shebang lines
answer_card.answer_md:
Two shebangs are officially supported:

```powershell
#!powershell
#!/usr/bin/pwsh
```

- `#!powershell`: Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility. Windows uses `powershell.exe` (5.1); Linux/macOS still use `/usr/bin/pwsh`. Use it for modules that must work on older Windows without PowerShell 7.
- `#!/usr/bin/pwsh`: PowerShell 7. Windows uses `pwsh.exe`; Linux/macOS use `/usr/bin/pwsh`. Use it for modules needing PowerShell 7+ features or cross-platform support.

Other shebangs pointing at `pwsh` on non-Windows may work but aren't officially supported or well tested. Prefer `#!/usr/bin/pwsh` and control the interpreter with `ansible_pwsh_interpreter`.
